title: Charge Disputes and Charge Corrections — Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)
content:
A patient may dispute a specific charge line on a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account.

## Filing window

A charge dispute is accepted only within the dispute filing window counted from the date of the first statement that listed the disputed charge. Count calendar days starting the day after that statement's posting date; a dispute logged on the last day of the window is accepted. The statement's posting date is read from the account's records.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, a window of 180 days).* If the first statement listing the charge posted on 1 March, day 180 is 28 August: a dispute logged on 28 August is accepted; one logged on 29 August is not.

## Logging and response

Each dispute is logged as a charge dispute inquiry naming the disputed charge line, at most the class's number of disputes per account (counted over the life of the account), and is answered within the class's dispute response in business days.

## Credits a representative may post

A representative may credit a disputed line when the account's records show the error:

- a duplicate of another line with the same chargemaster code, service date and units (credited without review where the terms auto-credit duplicates);
- units billed above the units documented;
- a supply that is not separately billable; or
- a service the encounter record shows was not rendered;

provided the credit does not exceed the representative credit authority. A larger credit is forwarded to coding review and is not posted by the representative. A charge line is credited at most once for the same reason.

## Effect on the patient balance

On a self-pay account already billed to the patient, the credited gross amount also reduces the patient balance by a charge correction adjustment equal to the credited amount less the uninsured discount already granted on it: the credited amount times one minus the discount percent that was applied, rounded half-up to the cent, sourced to the charge credit. On an insured account the credit produces a corrected claim to the payer and no patient-balance adjustment until the payer re-adjudicates.

*Worked figure (hypothetical).* A credit of 200.00 on a self-pay account billed with a 40 percent discount produces a charge correction adjustment of 200.00 times 0.60, that is 120.00.
